what: The room each flight read keeps across a flush is stated in rows (16,384) with a comment saying rows are `some hundred bytes each`; a SpanRow is 2,240 bytes, so each span table keeps 36.7 MiB. Keeping 256 KiB a table instead was built and measured: the profile holder's live heap at idle 64 to 76 MiB to 58 (one run), and a comment edit and run 22.7 to 26.6 ms on that binary, so it was taken out.
cost: one build, one run, two commits made and dropped
cause: a bound in rows over rows of very different sizes; and a flush that grows its buffers again is on something a request waits for, which was not looked into
state: open: the room should be by bytes, once growing it again costs a request nothing
